guide.summary: Linear documents user OAuth for apps that each connected person authorizes, and the default read scope covers read access to the user's account. That read scope supports reading issue titles through the GraphQL API with cursor pagination, so no write scope is needed.

steps.title: Read the first page of issue titles
steps.detail: Send the issues query with first: 10, includeArchived: true and pageInfo, using the OAuth Bearer access token from exchange-authorization-code. Representative input: the access_token value. Titles are returned at data.issues.nodes[].title, the list of node objects inside data.issues. The continuation cursor is data.issues.pageInfo.endCursor, and hasNextPage is in the same pageInfo object. Boundary check: the body is a query with no mutation, selects only id, title and pageInfo, and the token must carry only the read scope rather than issues:create or write.
steps.doneWhen: HTTP 200 with data.issues.nodes[].title values and data.issues.pageInfo.hasNextPage and endCursor present. Boundary check: the request body contains no mutation and no issue is created or updated.

evidence.quote: } ``` To query the next 10, simply pass the value of `pageInfo.endCursor` as `after` parameter for the next request. You can do this as long as `pageInfo.hasNextPage` return true
#### Archived resources Archived resources are hidden by default from the paginated responses. They can be included by passing optional `includeArchived: true` as a query parameter for pagination.
* `read` - (Default) Read access for the user's account. This scope will always be present.

request.example: curl 'https://api.linear.app/graphql' '-X' 'POST' '-H' 'Content-Type: application/json' '-H' 'Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>' '--data' '{"query":"query { issues(first: 10, includeArchived: true) { nodes { id title } pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } } }"}'

fields: ACCESS_TOKEN: access_token from exchange-authorization-code
Titles are at data.issues.nodes[].title
Next cursor is at data.issues.pageInfo.endCursor
includeArchived: true included so archived issues are returned

steps.title: Read the next page of issue titles using endCursor
steps.detail: Repeat the same query with includeArchived: true and after set to the prior response's data.issues.pageInfo.endCursor, keeping first: 10. Repeat with each newly returned endCursor until data.issues.pageInfo.hasNextPage is false. That false value is the documented stopping condition, and two pages alone do not complete the listing. Collect data.issues.nodes[].title from every page. Boundary check: each request is a query only, and the token's read scope is the only grant in use.
steps.doneWhen: Every page is requested by passing the prior endCursor as after until pageInfo.hasNextPage is false, with titles collected from each page. Boundary check: the outgoing request log contains only these query requests and no issueCreate or issueUpdate mutation.

evidence.quote: } ``` To query the next 10, simply pass the value of `pageInfo.endCursor` as `after` parameter for the next request. You can do this as long as `pageInfo.hasNextPage` return true
and you'll paginate through all the values in the collection.
#### Archived resources Archived resources are hidden by default from the paginated responses. They can be included by passing optional `includeArchived: true` as a query parameter for pagination.

fields: END_CURSOR: data.issues.pageInfo.endCursor from the previous response

includeArchived: true kept on every page
